subject: Quiet Labs: discovery recap & proposed reconnection
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quiet Labs: discovery recap & proposed reconnection

Team — quick thread to align before I reach back to Quiet Labs. Short context and suggested next steps below.

What happened
- Discovery call on 2027-04-13 with Samir (Head of ML) + procurement loop. Good engagement; positive on latency/cost conversation but they have competing priorities for Q2.
- I followed up twice (4/15 and 4/16) with no response so far. HubSpot shows views but no replies.

Top asks from discovery
- Proof of predictable inference latency for 1K qps (their use case: inference at edge of exchange workflows)
- Data residency / compliance: SOC2 + VPC/private plane assurances
- Rough pricing for a 6-month pilot (dedicated pool) and SOW/next steps for procurement

Why I want alignment before a bump
- Their procurement team is sensitive to commercial language — we should have a clear SOW + security note before we nudge again.
- Technical call offer (SE-led) will materially increase response rate; want Dev to own the ask.

Proposed next steps (my plan)
1) Dev: confirm the core technical ask (latency numbers, sample config to propose). Can you provide a 2-line technical summary I can send?
2) Marissa: outline a compact success plan we can include in the bump (3 milestones).
3) Leadership: Laura, if there's any discretion on pilot pricing / trial capacity we should offer, flag it here.
4) If we agree, I'll send a short, personalized bump to Samir (draft below) and include SOW draft + security note.

Draft bump I'm planning (need greenlight):
---
Subject: Quick check — pilot plan & SOW for Quiet Labs
Samir — circling back after our call. We know timing shifts; if Quiet Labs is still evaluating execution options, we'd be happy to: 1) run a short latency demo on a representative query set, 2) share a concise SOW for procurement, and 3) provide a security note for your compliance team. If that sounds useful, I can schedule a 30-min SE workshop this week.
---

Attachments I plan to include: QuietLabs-SOW-draft.pdf, discovery-notes-quietlabs.txt

Please reply with quick one-line approvals or edits. If I don't hear back by EOD tomorrow I'll still send the bump but will tailor based on the responses here.

Thanks — Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(h) 415-555-0132

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 11:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quiet Labs: discovery recap & proposed reconnection

+1 on the approach, Hannah. A few technical clarifications to include in the bump (keeps the procurement questions minimal):
- Latency baseline: with our natively batched runtime on an a100-like pool, p50 gen latency for their typical 512-token workload is ~35-45ms when batched to 8. P95 sits ~120-160ms depending on sequence tail. We should avoid absolute p99 claims without a live demo.
- Pilot recommendation: propose a short 48–72 hour latency validation run using a small dataset they provide (we can remote-execute against a dedicated pool). That gives them deterministic numbers for procurement.
- Security blurb: we have SOC2 and can offer VPC/private control plane; but for on-prem we need a longer procurement window — call that out.

I can put together a one-paragraph technical note and an ops checklist (what we need from Quiet Labs to run the 48–72 hour validation) by EOD. Suggest we include that as a single-page PDF with the bump.

— Dev
Staff Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quiet Labs: discovery recap & proposed reconnection

Thanks for looping us, Hannah. From a CS perspective we should make the path to initial value explicit so procurement sees tangible milestones. Proposed 3-point success plan to include in the bump / SOW:
1) Week 0–1: Discovery handoff + dataset transfer (we'll provide a secure presigned upload)
2) Week 1: 48–72 hour latency validation (Dev-led) with a short report and recommended production config
3) Week 2–8: Pilot (dedicated pool) with weekly checkpoints; adoption metrics: p50/p95 latency, cost per 1k tokens, error rate, and a short exec summary at the end.

If Quiet Labs needs an accounting-friendly billing cadence, we can propose a two-pay milestone (validation + pilot) — that's often acceptable for procurement.

I can draft a single-page success plan to attach. Also note: if marketing or legal needs to be looped, let's surface names now so they don't block later.

— Marissa
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@quietlabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Quick check — pilot plan & SOW for Quiet Labs

Samir — following up on our discussion last week. Wanted to share a short plan that would make procurement and your compliance team comfortable without a heavy lift on your side.

TL;DR: we can run a tight 48–72 hour latency validation on a dedicated pool (we'll run on your sample data), provide a single-page technical note and a concise SOW for procurement. After validation, we can transition to a 6-week pilot with weekly checkpoints.

If you're still evaluating, would you be open to a 30-minute SE workshop this week to confirm the dataset and run scope? If you prefer a short SOW and security note first, I've attached both.

Attachments: QuietLabs-SOW-draft.pdf, discovery-notes-quietlabs.txt
